subject: P06
required_fixes: P06-R2-F1 (high): Do not dispatch deferred work while draining an export after stop. In crates/desktop-core/src/harness/session.rs:962-964, cancellation enters finish_export; that function calls the ordinary on_frame handler at :1008. Its HistoryRead failure arm (:1300-1305) clears reading and immediately executes self.deferred through on_command. A next Send can legitimately have been deferred while the previous export was pending (:1132-1138; authority/harness_domain.rs admits it while progress is Ready). If End/Sleep/Quit then begins and the export refusal arrives during the grace period, on_command queues turn/start (:1226) after cancellation. The writer drains queued frames even when its sender is dropped (:838-849), so stopping can dispatch a new inference turn instead of cancelling that pending message. Make export draining stop-specific: it must not release deferred Send/Renew commands or admit fresh effects. Acceptance: hold an export, queue the next message, initiate stop, then return an export refusal during the grace window; observe no additional turn/start or Gateway request, no restart and no replay after reconnect. Retain truthful local status for the unsent message.

P06-R2-F2 (high): Retain the unsaved-transcript obligation across an export error during the grace period. With no deferred command, a HistoryRead refusal handled by finish_export clears reading (:1301) without saving. A malformed HistoryRead result likewise clears reading before validating its context/replay (:1278-1284), and finish_export discards the resulting error. launched then computes turn_open only from turn/read state (:522); both are None, all entries are settled, and the fallback at :573-578 is skipped. A first completed conversation is lost, or an older record remains without its latest turn. The refusal sets saveFailure, but the malformed-result path can end without even that failure indication. Track whether the current transcript was actually saved independently of the pending-request flag. If export draining fails, seal the latest transcript inspect-only without an older or fabricated replay and report relevant failures. Acceptance: after a completed turn, stop and deliver a refusal or malformed export within the grace period, on both a first turn and an existing record; offline inspection must retain the exact latest entries/outcomes, continuation must be refused without a matching replay, and reconnect must send nothing.
evidence_gaps: P06-R2-G1: The new pending-export tests exercise an export that stays silent, leaving reading set, and an ordinary real-engine export. They do not deliver a refusal/malformed result during finish_export or include a deferred message when stopping. Add deterministic production-interface coverage for both required fixes and verify the emitted engine frames/remote request counts as well as protected offline history. The new C20 mutation removes reading from the fallback condition; it does not test these error/drain transitions.
limitations: Independent read-only cumulative re-review. No source changes, test/build reruns, application/engine launches, product endpoint calls or credential access. Findings follow the production call graph and state transitions; they are not claimed as newly executed runtime reproductions. Only the designated verdict artifact is written.

The remediation covers the previously identified silent-export window: finish_export waits up to three seconds, an outstanding read marks work for fallback saving, and unanswered-export timeout now retains inspect-only history. Added tests cover first and previously saved conversations offline, continuation refusal and no automatic engine relaunch. However, consuming an error during the new grace period clears that fallback flag and can run the ordinary handler's deferred work. Architecture remains focused; behavior, stop authority and validation remain below the gate for these specific transitions.
